name: Kaggle Notebooks
tagline: The last free P100 standing — no credit card, no subscription, just a 12-hour session cap and a queue when everyone else is training too.
quota: Free GPU: 1x NVIDIA Tesla P100 per notebook (16 GB), or 2x NVIDIA Tesla T4 (T4 x2). A TPU v3-8 is also free. Each accelerator comes with 4 CPU cores and 29 GB of RAM. Verbatim from the docs: "You can add a single NVIDIA Tesla P100 to your Notebook for free."
limits: 12 hours execution time for CPU and GPU notebook sessions (9 hours for TPU). Interactive sessions end after 20 minutes of idle time. Free GPU availability is limited and you may be queued at busy times. No weekly GPU hour quota is published for standard free accounts — only the per-session caps above. Colab Pro / Pro+ subscribers get 15 and 30 extra GPU hours per week on Kaggle.
expiry: No depleting balance and no published weekly quota for the standard free tier. Limits are per-session (12h run / 20min idle), so capacity effectively resets each time you start a new session.
path: Create a free Kaggle account → open Notebooks → New Notebook → right-hand Settings panel → Accelerator → choose GPU P100 or GPU T4 x2 → run the cell below to confirm what you actually got.
code:
import subprocess, torch
print(subprocess.run(['nvidia-smi'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout)
print('CUDA available:', torch.cuda.is_available())
print('Device:', torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'none')
print('VRAM GB:', torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory / 1e9 if torch.cuda.is_available() else 0)
verdict: The most generous genuinely free GPU left in 2026: a full P100 for 12 straight hours with no card and no paid plan. The real catches are queueing at peak hours, a 20-minute idle timeout that kills interactive sessions, and no published weekly quota — so Kaggle can tighten access dynamically without ever changing a number on a pricing page.
best_for: Fine-tuning small-to-medium models (7B LoRA fits comfortably)
Learning PyTorch/CUDA without owning a GPU or a card

name: Modal
tagline: $30/month of serverless GPU credit that actually buys real H100 minutes — and you only pay while your code is running.
quota: Starter plan is $0/month and includes $30/month of free compute credit. Also included: 100 concurrent containers, 10 GPU concurrency, 200 deployed apps, 3 workspace seats, 1 TiB/month free block storage, region selection, scheduled and web functions (limited). GPU menu spans T4, L4, A10, L40S, A100-40GB, A100-80GB, RTX PRO 6000, H100, H200, B200 and B300.
limits: 100 containers and 10 GPU concurrency on Starter. Log retention 1 day. 5 deployed cron jobs. Non-preemptible execution costs 3x base price. Non-default regions cost 1.5-1.75x base price. Reference GPU rates: T4 $0.000164/sec, L4 $0.000222/sec, A10 $0.000306/sec, L40S $0.000542/sec, A100-40GB $0.000583/sec, A100-80GB $0.000694/sec, H100 $0.001097/sec, H200 $0.001261/sec, B200 $0.001736/sec, B300 $0.001972/sec.
expiry: $30 of credit resets every calendar month. Unused credit does not roll over.
region: Global (region selection included; some regions billed at 1.5-1.75x base rates)
path: Sign up at modal.com/signup — the $0 Starter plan ships with $30/month of credit → pip install modal → modal setup → save the file below as gpu_check.py → modal run gpu_check.py to launch a real GPU container from your laptop.
verdict: The best dollar-for-GPU free tier in 2026 if you are willing to write Python instead of clicking around notebooks: $30/month reaches everything from T4 up to B300, billed per second with zero idle cost. The hard limitation is that Modal is pure serverless — you get containers, not a persistent machine, so it suits batch jobs, inference endpoints and short fine-tunes far better than interactive tinkering or long training runs.
best_for: Serverless inference endpoints and model APIs
Batch jobs: embeddings, transcription, image generation
Short fine-tunes and eval sweeps where per-second billing wins

name: Lightning AI Studios
tagline: A free 4-CPU Studio plus a grab-bag of GPU credits whose size Lightning no longer publishes — worth an account, not worth planning around.
quota: Every account gets 1 free 4-CPU Studio to code and run workloads in, plus the first 10 GB of Drive storage free. Eligible free-plan users also receive complimentary credits that can be spent on compute, inference and storage, including GPUs. Verbatim: "Users get 1 free 4-CPU Studio to code in and run workloads on." The docs give no dollar or hour figure for the free credits.
limits: Only one Studio is free; any additional CPU Studio or any GPU machine is billed at listed rates and consumes credits, billed per second. Storage above 10 GB costs $0.10/GB/month (billed daily); free accounts cap out at 50 GB total in Drive. Credit conversion is 1 credit = $1 (e.g. a GPU at 1.17 credits/hr equals $1.17/hr).
expiry: Verbatim: "Free credits are promotional, non-transferable, and do not accumulate." Lightning also states it "may change or limit free credit grants, eligibility, usage rules, or expiration terms at any time." Purchased credits expire after 1 year.
path: Sign up at lightning.ai → open your free 4-CPU Studio → open a terminal and run the snippet below → to spend credits on a GPU, start a Studio or Job with a GPU machine and watch the credit burn rate in the dashboard.
code:
import subprocess, torch
print(subprocess.run(['nvidia-smi', '-L'], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout or 'no GPU attached to this Studio')
print('CUDA available:', torch.cuda.is_available())
if torch.cuda.is_available():
    print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(0), torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory / 1e9, 'GB')
verdict: Genuinely free to enter — one always-on 4-CPU Studio costs nothing — but the GPU side is now deliberately vague: Lightning's own billing docs say eligible users get "complimentary credits" without ever publishing how many, and reserve the right to change the grant at any time. Treat the GPU hours as a welcome bonus you discover after signup, not a quota you can plan a project around.
best_for: A permanent free cloud dev box with 4 CPUs
Testing whether Lightning's workflow fits you before paying
Short GPU experiments if your account happens to get a usable grant

name: Replicate
tagline: Not a free tier anymore, but a curated sandbox: a handful of image and video models run free until Replicate taps you on the shoulder for a card.
quota: No standing free credit. Replicate's billing docs still carry a "Free limits" section: "You can run select models on Replicate for free, but after a bit you'll be asked to set up billing." The free set is a curated collection at replicate.com/collections/try-for-free, currently ~11 models including google/imagen-4, black-forest-labs/flux-1.1-pro, flux-dev, flux-kontext-pro, ideogram-v3-turbo, minimax/video-01, luma/reframe-video, topazlabs/video-upscale, topazlabs/image-upscale, codeformer and gfpgan.
limits: No numeric free limit is published — you get "a bit" of free usage, then billing setup is required. Once billing is on, everything is pay-as-you-go per second by hardware: T4 $0.000225/sec, L40S $0.000975/sec, A100-80GB $0.001400/sec, H100 $0.001525/sec, H200 $0.001525/sec. Public models bill only active processing time (setup and idle are free); private models and deployments bill setup + idle + active. Some features are billing-gated.
expiry: Free usage is a one-time onboarding allowance, not a recurring monthly grant. It ends when Replicate asks you to set up billing.
path: Go to replicate.com/collections/try-for-free → pick a listed model → run it from the web UI with no card while the allowance lasts → for anything else, add billing and call the API with the snippet below.
code:
import os, replicate

output = replicate.run(
    "black-forest-labs/flux-schnell",
    input={"prompt": "a lighthouse in a storm,35mm film still"},
)
print(output)  # requires REPLICATE_API_TOKEN + billing once free usage ends
verdict: Officially still free for a short, deliberately unspecified trial on a narrow model list — so it is fine for kicking the tires on Flux or Imagen, and useless as a real free GPU budget. If you want a number, there isn't one: Replicate removed the old documented free tier and now hides the limit behind "after a bit".
best_for: Trying Flux / Imagen / video models before committing a card
One-off image or video generation for a demo
Comparing model quality across providers cheaply
